newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 27.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Tuesday:
* "The Lost World: Jurassic Park," made by Seagram Co Ltd's Universal, broke nearly every box office record in its debut weekend, raking in $92.7 million.
* French stocks dropped nearly 4 percent after the left emerged victorious in the first round of the parliamentary election.
* At a meeting in Paris, economic ministers from the 29 nations in the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development expressed continued confidence in economic globalization.
* A survey by a temporary employment company has found that there are likely to be more job opportunities this summer.

* As the tobacco talks progress, a central question remains: Where should the lines be drawn between punishing tobacco companies, compensating victims and encouraging cigarette makers to act with more restraint in the future?
* Expansion of the Greek merchant fleet has outpaced demand for cargo space, leading to troubles for shippers.
* A digital still camera Toshiba plans to start selling this summer may make it possible one day to develop a new type of image-capturing device that is a tiny camera-on-a-chip.
* Japan's automobile productin is expected to continue growing in the months ahead.
* Congress is expected to soon launch an effort to overhaul and redesign Medicare.
* Russian gas monopoly Gazprom is seeking to raise between $2 billion and $3 billion in financing from Western capital markets.
* Fred Wilson, the founder of Flatiron Partners, a venture capital firm that specializes in Internet-related companies, sees "the real emergence of a business."
* Gordon Brown, Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer, has shaken things up after less than a month in the post.
* A slump in technology companies, a bevy of which went public in the past two years, has been sharper than analysts expected.
* Swiss pharmaceutical giant Roche Holding Ltd plans to buy Boehringer Mannheim GmH, a German maker of drugs and diagnostic products, for about $11 billion.

* As they prepare for a new series of air pollution controls to be issued by the Environmental Protection Agency, American companies are shying away from the usual tactic of offering gloom and doom financial assessments of the rules.
